To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intercultural kindergarten education is a complex phenomenon, and that it is important for teacher education to be aware of this.

the intercultural teacher education program is a good starting point, but that the teacher educators should pay more attention to the ethical aspects of interculturability and that the teacher educators and the student teachers should pay more attention on the intercultural aspects of the Finnish society.
the student teachers in the study did not have an intercultural perspective on the world, but that they were able to develop one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discursive relationships that constitute intercultural teacher education and how these relationships can be understood as a political project.
the question of how to teach intercultural teacher education in a way that does not reproduce the same discursive relationships of interculturability that have been dominant in the past.
the ways in which teacher education is being reconfigured by interculturality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interculturality is not a straightforward concept and it is not a simple task to teach it to student teachers.
interculturality should not only be a goal of the teacher education program, but should be a goal of all higher education programs.
interculturality is a complex concept that requires a critical and reflexive approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teacher educators in this study are not able to provide a strong enough argument to justify their intercultural agenda in their teacher education.
interculturality is not only a question of knowledge, skills, and attitudes, but a question of desire and politics.

the discursive construction of the interculturality agenda is not yet fully developed in Finland, and the discursive relationships of intercultural teacher education are still in the process of being constructed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intercultural teacher education should be based on the idea of ethical interculturality.
interculturality cannot be understood as a neutral concept, but is always embedded in power relations and politics.
interculturality cannot be reduced to an instrumental goal in teacher education.
